metadata.title: Why the Drug Reached the Tumor and the Tumor Still Grew Back
metadata.purpose: vox-explainer slate cut of Cancer Nanomedicine candidate 06. Source: cancer-nanomedicine/chapters/02-tumor-transport-barriers.md (outward interstitial fluid pressure mechanism and inside-out regrowth only).
metadata.color_semantics: TEAL #1F6F5C = drug / particles accumulating at the rim; CRIMSON #BF3339 = unreached core / outward pressure / regrowth; GOLD #F5D061 = the pressure-gradient highlight (fill only, never text)
metadata.note: EXCLUSIONS: diffusion limit derivation (1-2mm threshold), four-barrier list, 30-vs-150nm size debate, and radiation resistance. Keep ONLY: the outward-pressure mechanism (leaky vessels + no lymphatics -> fluid buildup -> net outward flow -> particles pushed back to rim) and the inside-out regrowth payoff (hypoxic core survives, selection for resistant cells, tumor regrows from core).

props.command: Why the Drug Reached the Tumor and the Tumor Still Grew Back?

beats.narration_text: This is Liam, in for Bear. A nanoparticle drug reaches a mouse tumor. The vessels are leaky — particles accumulate. The outer rim clears beautifully. Weeks later, the tumor doubles in volume — growing from the inside out.

lines: Why the Drug Reached the Tumor and the Tumor Still Grew Back
props.sub: the outward-pressure paradox — accumulation is not delivery

card.copy: Why the Drug Reached the Tumor and the Tumor Still Grew Back
card.sub: the outward-pressure paradox — accumulation is not delivery

beats.new_visual_element: [TITLE] drug reaches tumor — tumor doubles from the inside

beats.narration_text: MRI shows a two-millimeter viable core at week three. The drug was there. The whole-organ measurement said it had accumulated. The core is untouched. Then the core grows back.

production_viz.label: MRI-like schematic — dead rim, viable core
production_viz.mechanic: circular tumor cross-section: dark outer ring (drug-killed rim) + lighter central circle (viable core). Crimson dashed annotation ring around the core with label 'viable core, ~2 mm'. Sub-label 'whole-organ signal: drug accumulated'.
production_viz.note: sets the paradox visually — accumulated but core untouched

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] MRI schematic — dark rim, viable core ringed

beats.narration_text: A drug reaches the tumor. Vessels are leaky and particles accumulate. The outer rim is cleared. Weeks later, the tumor regrows from the inside. The drug was there. Why did the core survive?

card.copy: The drug reached the tumor. The rim was cleared. The tumor regrew from the inside.

beats.new_visual_element: [CARD] the question — why did the core survive?

build.needs: SCRIPTING GAP — B03 has no drawable spec. Author a diagram, a Remotion pattern, or a Manim scene. Do not fill this with generated media.

beats.narration_text: The naive picture: leaky vessels let particles in, and particles spread inward through the tissue. That is not wrong — it is just half the story. The same leaky vessels create a second effect no one celebrates.

production_viz.label: leaky vessel + inward diffusion (half the story)
production_viz.mechanic: a horizontal vessel wall with gaps (leaks) at the top; teal particle dots exit the gaps and drift downward into tissue space. Label 'leaky vessels' above the vessel, 'particles diffuse inward' below. A crimson question mark hovers to the right captioned 'the other effect →'.
production_viz.note: the incomplete mental model — sets up the reversal

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] leaky vessel with particles diffusing inward — half the story

beats.narration_text: Leaky vessel walls pour fluid into the tumor faster than the lymphatic system can drain it. Tumor lymphatics are broken or absent. The fluid has nowhere to go — so it stays, and pressure builds.

production_viz.label: leaky vessel in + broken lymphatic out = fluid stays
production_viz.mechanic: vessel at top pouring blue fluid drops into a tumor box; a lymphatic drain at the bottom marked with a red X (broken). Fluid level rises inside the box; a small pressure gauge on the right ticks upward as fluid rises. Labels: 'in: leaky vessel', 'out: broken lymphatic', 'pressure ↑'.
production_viz.note: core physics: what enters cannot leave

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] leaky vessel in + broken lymphatic out — pressure rises

beats.narration_text: Fluid moves down pressure gradients. The tumor core accumulates fluid and reaches pressures five to ten times higher than normal tissue. Net flow is outward — from the pressurized core toward the tumor edge. A particle trying to move inward is swimming against that current.

production_viz.label: pressure gradient: core high, rim low — net outward flow
production_viz.mechanic: circular tumor cross-section with a gold-filled radial gradient (dense center → sparse rim). Small pressure gauge in the core reading '25 mmHg', another at the rim reading '5 mmHg'. Crimson radial arrows point outward from core to rim. Bottom caption: 'net flow is outward — 5–10× normal pressure'.
production_viz.note: the pressure asymmetry — the whole mechanism in one image

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] radial pressure gradient — core 25 vs rim 5 mmHg, arrows outward

beats.narration_text: So particles extravasate near the rim vessels, and the outward current carries them back. They pile up at the periphery. The core stays particle-free — not because the EPR effect failed, but because it succeeded and then the pressure it created pushed the particles away.

production_viz.label: particles enter at rim vessels, get carried back outward
production_viz.mechanic: tumor cross-section with rim vessels drawn as short teal arcs on the outer boundary. Teal particle dots exit the vessels inward briefly, then curve back outward along crimson flow arrows and accumulate as a dense teal band at the periphery. Empty core in the center. Label 'pile-up at rim' in TEAL, 'core stays particle-free' in CRIMSON.
production_viz.note: the payoff of the mechanism — the paradox visualized

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] particles enter at rim, get carried back — teal band at periphery

beats.narration_text: That unreached core is also hypoxic — starved of oxygen. Hypoxia selects for cells that tolerate stress, evade death signals, and survive. The cells the drug never reached are not a random sample. They are the tumor's most resistant survivors.

production_viz.label: hypoxic core selects for resistant cells
production_viz.mechanic: tumor cross-section: rim cells drawn as small teal dots (drug reached). Core drawn as gray hypoxic zone with an oxygen icon crossed out ('O₂ ↓'). Inside the core, a few cells drawn in bold CRIMSON with a chain-link resistance icon and label 'stress-tolerant · drug-resistant'. Bottom caption: 'not a random sample — the survivors'.
production_viz.note: selection pressure — the second half of the paradox

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] hypoxic core with resistant survivor cells highlighted

beats.narration_text: The rim cells the drug killed were not the cells most likely to cause recurrence. The core cells it never reached were — and the hypoxic pressure had spent months making them harder to kill.

production_viz.label: highlight quote card — the inside-out selection
production_viz.mechanic: editorial quote card, cream ground, EB Garamond serif italic text: 'The rim cells the drug killed were not the ones most likely to cause recurrence. The core cells it never reached were.' A gold highlighter bar under 'core cells it never reached'. Attribution 'Cancer Nanomedicine · ch. 02' in small MONO.
production_viz.note: the memorable sentence — the punchline in one card

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] highlight quote — the ones the drug never reached

beats.narration_text: Take an illustrative scenario. A nanoparticle therapy shrinks a mouse tumor rim by sixty percent over three weeks. At week three, IFP at the core measures twenty-five millimeters of mercury. At the rim: five. The core — viable, two millimeters across — sits behind a pressure wall the particles cannot cross. By week eight, tumor volume has doubled. The growth originates from the core.

production_viz.label: two-panel timeline — week 3 vs week 8
production_viz.mechanic: left panel 'WEEK 3': shrunken tumor cross-section with a 60% rim shrink note (TEAL 'rim −60%'), viable core 2 mm ringed CRIMSON, two gauges: 'core IFP 25 mmHg' / 'rim IFP 5 mmHg'. Right panel 'WEEK 8': tumor drawn 2× larger, arrows from core radiating outward, caption 'volume 2×, origin: core' in CRIMSON. Footer label 'illustrative scenario'.
production_viz.note: worked example — the numbers are illustrative, labeled as such

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] week 3 → week 8 timeline — rim shrinks, core doubles

beats.narration_text: The drug reached the tumor. The leaky vessels that let it in also flooded the interstitium and drove fluid outward. Particles stayed at the rim. The core survived, selected for resistance, and grew back. The accumulation was real. The delivery was not.

card.copy: The accumulation was real. The delivery was not.
card.sub: leaky vessels → outward pressure → particles at rim → hypoxic core survives and regrows

beats.narration_text: The drug reached the tumor and the delivery still failed. Leaky vessels flood the interstitium; broken lymphatics cannot drain it; core pressure runs five to ten times normal, and net flow is outward. Particles pile at the rim. The unreached hypoxic core selects for the tumor's most resistant cells, and grows back. Accumulation is not delivery.

artifactLines: Leaky vessels + broken lymphatics build core interstitial pressure 5–10× normal.
Net flow is outward — particles that extravasate get carried back to the rim.
The unreached hypoxic core selects for stress-tolerant, drug-resistant cells.
Rim shrinks ~60%; core IFP 25 vs rim 5 mmHg; tumor doubles by week 8 from the core.
The drug arrived. The delivery failed. Accumulation is not delivery.
